classification.difficultyReason: Factorise a consecutive range of whole numbers and recognise the primes within it.

content.prompt: Show that each of the whole numbers between 28 and 37 can be written as the product of prime numbers.

answer.short: $28=2\times2\times7$; $29$ is prime; $30=2\times3\times5$; $31$ is prime; $32=2\times2\times2\times2\times2$; $33=3\times11$; $34=2\times17$; $35=5\times7$; $36=2\times2\times3\times3$; $37$ is prime.
answer.worked:
Split composite factors until every factor is prime. A prime number is already a product consisting of one prime factor.

$$\begin{align*}28&=2\times14\\28&=2\times2\times7\\30&=2\times15\\30&=2\times3\times5\\32&=2\times16\\32&=2\times2\times2\times2\times2\\33&=3\times11\\34&=2\times17\\35&=5\times7\\36&=4\times9\\36&=2\times2\times3\times3\end{align*}$$

$29$, $31$ and $37$ are prime: none is divisible by $2$, $3$ or $5$, the only primes less than or equal to their square roots.
